body:
Completed native verification on 2026-10-05.

Build/contract
- Installed native executable: C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\apps\desktop\release\win-unpacked\Hermes.exe
- Hermes CLI: v0.21.5+2168.g59004a6 (2026.9.24), upstream 59004a62; install method git.
- Release app.asar SHA-256: 3256ffd87ccd7153081cf27d5c8fefc82aff0037d9697220468f4a3728d854cf.
- Desktop build metadata: apps/desktop/dist/hermes-build.json; outputHash 5d3115a7d1716927e30d6ed699b09d048570e1f556fc2a747ee4aa11342cc357; win32/x64, Node 26.7.0.
- Contract verified from the installed source: standalone runtime entry is <HERMES_HOME>/desktop-plugins/<id>/plugin.js; plain ESM; imports limited to @hermes/plugin-sdk and react/react/jsx-runtime; default export needs id + register(ctx); routes use ROUTES_AREA and optional sidebar.nav contribution; enable/disable is live in Capabilities > Plugins.

Reusable POC
- Source changed only in C:\Users\User\.codex\worktrees\hermes-native-poc\Waystation\integrations\hermes\desktop\plugin.js.
- It registers id waystation-native-load-poc, route /waystation-native-poc, sidebar label Waystation POC, and a clearly labeled page. It has no ledger, worker, profile-state, or monitor connection.
- Installed copy used for the run: C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\hermes\desktop-plugins\waystation-native-load-poc\plugin.js. Source and installed copy matched SHA-256 d256b6dae863546935b1ff1c365249a9288bac0c3ec51bb767c15d1dd10c6395.

Exact repeat/undo
1. Copy integrations/hermes/desktop/plugin.js to <HERMES_HOME>\desktop-plugins\waystation-native-load-poc\plugin.js (create the folder).
2. In native Hermes open Capabilities > Plugins; the row appears disabled because defaultEnabled=false. Toggle Desktop: Waystation native-load POC on.
3. The sidebar row Waystation POC appears. Open it.
4. Disable the same Desktop toggle; the sidebar row disappears and the page contribution is removed.
5. Click Uninstall: Waystation native-load POC, or delete that one folder. The native app showed the toast “Waystation native-load POC uninstalled.” The folder was then absent and the desktop-plugins root was empty/removed.

Observed native result
- I launched the installed release artifact in a separate temporary Electron user-data directory with --remote-debugging-port=9224 so existing Hermes data was not used or changed. This was still the installed native Windows Hermes build, not a browser preview.
- In the actual native Hermes renderer, Plugins showed the POC row; enabling it produced the visible sidebar row “Waystation POC”; opening it visibly rendered “Waystation native-load POC”, “PROOF OF CONCEPT — this page is loaded from an external runtime desktop plugin.”, “No Waystation ledger, worker binding, or production monitor is connected.”, and the plugin id/route line.
- Disabling removed the sidebar entry. Uninstall removed the plugin row/folder and displayed the uninstall toast.

Preservation/limitations
- Existing default Hermes app data was not used by the test instance. C:\Users\User\AppData\Roaming\Hermes\Preferences remained 16,268 bytes with its pre-run timestamp; no config.yaml/state.db/ledger was modified.
- The temporary POC user-data directory was removed after the run. The installed plugin folder was removed. No Hermes core files, production Waystation ledger, worker bindings, or multi-project monitor were changed.
- This proves the minimal native page-loading contract only. It does not prove agent-plugin packaging, backend APIs, durable registry state, ledger synchronization, or production Monitor behavior.
